ai.description: This gecko reaches 80 mm SVL. It features a pale brown body with 6–8 dark transverse bands and a distinct white nuchal collar. Key traits include strongly curved toes and a granular dorsal texture.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus fasciolatus* is best distinguished by the presence of 3–4 distinct, dark brown transverse bands on the body, which are significantly narrower than the interspaces.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus fasciolatus* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found on tree trunks or rocks at mid-to-high elevations.
ai.behavior: The Banded Bent-toed Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to actively forage for small insects and invertebrates along rocky surfaces and tree trunks.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus fasciolatus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, spanning from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus fasciolatus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at mid-to-high elevations.
